newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-DRUT SAYS 1998 WORLD CUP NOT IN DANGER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DRUT SAYS 1998 WORLD CUP NOT IN DANGER.

text.p: French Sports Minister Guy Drut said on Wednesday there was no danger of France not hosting the 1998 World Cup finals.

"The World Cup will take place in France," Drut told parliament as the European Commission in Brussels stepped up legal moves against the way the country awarded contracts for the new showpiece Stade de France.

The commission sent France a "reasoned opinion", last stage before a disputed case goes to the European Court of Justice, for its incorrect application of EU public works rules related to the new stadium being built at Saint-Denis outside Paris.
"This element (the reasoned opinion) does not in any way cast doubt over the validity of the contract," he said.
"The previous government chose the most appropriate technical solution to ensure the completion (of the stadium) in the best conditions," Drut added.

A EU report on how the contracts were awarded and on which the commission acted could force the whole financial set-up of the Paris stadium to be reconsidered and the public cost to be dramatically increased.
The 80,000-seater Stade de France, due to be completed in November and officialy opened in January 1998, is scheduled to host the World Cup opening match and final.
